title: Free Hosting Options That Actually Work for a Blog (Tested)
html:
Most lists of "free web hosting" recommend unusable traps: dead cPanel hosts that inject ugly ads into your header, give you 500 MB of disk space, and crash with a 503 error as soon as ten people read your article. If you want genuine, fast, zero-cost hosting in 2026, you have to use developer edge platforms that serve pre-rendered static sites. I tested the top four platforms—Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Vercel Hobby, and Netlify—with real blog workloads. Here is what actually works, what breaks, and the hidden commercial traps to avoid.

Last updated: 13 Nov 2026. All plan limits, bandwidth caps, terms of service clauses, and overage fees cited below are verified against active platform documentation as of November 2026.

The Myth of "Free cPanel Hosting"

Before looking at developer platforms, let's address traditional free PHP/cPanel web hosts (like InfinityFree or the old 000webhost). Beginners often pick them because they want a classic WordPress dashboard. In reality, they are almost universally disastrous for three reasons:

  1. Aggressive Resource Throttling: Free shared hosts allocate around 10% to 20% of a single CPU core. Running a single WordPress plugin update or receiving 15 simultaneous visitors triggers CPU quota exhaustion, displaying a "CPU Limit Reached" error.
  2. Forced Subdomains or Injected Ads: Many free hosts force you to use subdomains like yoursite.freehost.com or silently inject pop-up ad scripts into your HTML, instantly killing your brand credibility and search rankings.
  3. Zero Uptime Guarantees: Free databases frequently drop connections. If your database goes down while Googlebot crawls your site, your pages get de-indexed.

If you want real reliability without paying ₹12,000+ per year on GoDaddy, the only legitimate solution is static site hosting on global Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).

The 4 Real Free Platforms Compared (Head-to-Head)

Here is how the four leading developer platforms compare across actual production limits:

Feature / Limit Cloudflare Pages GitHub Pages Vercel Hobby Netlify Free
Monthly Bandwidth Unlimited / Unmetered 100 GB (Soft limit) 100 GB 100 GB
Commercial / AdSense Allowed? Yes (100% permitted) Grey area (no e-commerce) NO (Strictly personal) Yes
Monthly Build Limits 500 builds / month 10 builds / hour 6,000 build mins / mo 300 build mins / mo
Custom Domains & SSL Free automatic Universal SSL Free Let's Encrypt SSL Free automatic SSL Free automatic SSL
Native 301 Redirects Yes (via _redirects) No (requires HTML meta hacks) Yes (via next.config / vercel.json) Yes (via _redirects)
Custom HTTP Headers Yes (via _headers) No Yes Yes (via _headers)
Surprise Bill Risk Zero (No credit card needed) Zero Medium (Account lock / upgrade) High ($55 per 100 GB overage)

1. Cloudflare Pages: The Undisputed Winner for Blogs

Cloudflare Pages is the platform that powers TrendsWheel. If you run an editorial blog, news site, or technical documentation, Cloudflare Pages is currently unbeatable on the free tier.

What Works Great:

  • Unmetered Edge Bandwidth: Unlike competitors that cap you at 100 GB, Cloudflare does not meter your bandwidth. If an article goes viral on Reddit and gets 500,000 visitors in 48 hours, Cloudflare serves the cached static HTML without charging you a single rupee or throttling your traffic.
  • Fully Commercial & AdSense Friendly: Cloudflare explicitly permits commercial websites, affiliate blogs, and ad-supported publishers on the free tier.
  • Native SEO Control: You can drop a plain _redirects file into your public/ folder with up to 2,000 static 301 redirect rules, and a _headers file for cache policies and security headers.
  • Indian Edge Coverage: Cloudflare has data centers in Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, and Hyderabad, delivering static HTML to Indian visitors in under 30 to 50 milliseconds.

What Doesn't Work (The Limits):

  • Static Assets Only: You cannot run a live PHP server or MySQL database. Your site must compile to static HTML, CSS, and JS (such as Next.js with output: 'export' or Astro).
  • Project Limits: Maximum 20,000 files per project and 25 MB per file. For a blog with 150 to 500 posts, 20,000 files is more than enough space.

2. GitHub Pages: The Solid Developer Classic

GitHub Pages is built into every GitHub repository. It has been hosting developer blogs for over a decade, but it has distinct limitations that make it tricky for professional blogging.

What Works Great:

  • Zero Account Overhead: If your code is already on GitHub, you can publish a site straight from your repository settings with zero extra sign-ups.
  • Simple Workflow: Using GitHub Actions (like actions/deploy-pages), you can compile your Next.js project and deploy it automatically on every git push.
  • Free Custom Domains & SSL: Custom domains are simple to connect, and GitHub provisions Let's Encrypt certificates automatically.

What Doesn't Work (The Pitfalls):

  • No Server-Side Redirects: GitHub Pages does not support _redirects files. If you change a post URL, you cannot issue an authentic HTTP 301 Permanent Redirect. You have to use client-side HTML <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tags, which Google handles slowly and inefficiently.
  • No Custom Security Headers: You cannot set Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, or cache control headers at the web server level.
  • Bandwidth & Size Quotas: Repositories are recommended to stay under 1 GB, and monthly bandwidth has a soft ceiling of 100 GB.

3. Vercel Hobby: Superb Developer Experience, But Beware the Commercial Trap

Vercel is the creator and maintainer of Next.js, and deploying a Next.js project on Vercel is the smoothest developer experience in the software industry. However, running a blog on Vercel's free Hobby plan comes with a massive catch that few YouTubers mention.

The Catch: Section 2.3 Commercial Use Restriction

Vercel's Terms of Service strictly define the Hobby tier as non-commercial personal use. If you place Google AdSense banners, promote Amazon or hosting affiliate links, or accept sponsored posts, your site is generating commercial revenue. Technically, running commercial monetization on Vercel Hobby violates their ToS.

To use Vercel commercially, you must upgrade to the Pro Plan at $20/user/month (~₹1,700/mo, or over ₹20,000 annually). If your goal in leaving expensive shared hosting was to save ₹12,000/year, paying ₹20,000/year on Vercel defeats the purpose.

What Works Great (For Non-Commercial Blogs):

  • Zero-config Next.js deployment: preview URLs for pull requests, instant edge rollouts, and automatic framework optimization.
  • Native image optimization API (up to 1,000 source images free per month).

4. Netlify Free: Generous Features with a Sneaky Overage Trap

Netlify pioneered the modern Jamstack movement and includes great built-in features like form handling and identity management. But their free tier has one dangerous rule you must watch out for.

The Catch: Automatic Bandwidth Overage Billing

Netlify provides 100 GB of free bandwidth per month. But unlike Cloudflare (which is unlimited) or GitHub Pages (which warns you), Netlify's billing system automatically charges your credit card $55 per 100 GB block if your traffic exceeds your quota.

If an article with high-resolution images goes viral on social media and transfers 350 GB of traffic in a month, you could face an unexpected bill of $110 to $165 (₹9,500 to ₹14,000) on what you thought was a "free" hosting plan.

What Works Great:

  • Built-in Form Handling: You can submit up to 100 contact forms per month natively into Netlify's dashboard without setting up an external backend or mail server.
  • First-Class Redirects: Supports _redirects and _headers out of the box with query-parameter matching and proxy rules.

How We Replaced Dynamic Features for Free

When switching to free static hosting, you lose dynamic server-side backends. Here is how you replace them without spending money:

  1. Contact Forms: Use a free provider like Web3Forms or Formspree (both give 50 to 250 free monthly submissions), or use a clean spam-protected mailto: link.
  2. Site Search: Generate a lightweight search-index.json during your build. Browsers can download that 20 KB index and search hundreds of post titles in memory in 2 milliseconds with zero database load.
  3. Analytics: Combine Google Analytics 4 with Cloudflare's free privacy-first Web Analytics to track visitor journeys without performance penalties.

The Verdict: Which Free Host Should You Pick?

  • For Monetized Blogs & Content Sites: Pick Cloudflare Pages. It is the only platform offering unmetered bandwidth, commercial AdSense permission, and complete redirect control without charging a rupee. (Read our migration story, our Laravel vs Next.js hosting cost breakdown, and our guide to the cheapest way to host a blog in India under ₹75/mo).
  • For Open-Source Portfolios & Code Docs: Pick GitHub Pages. It integrates directly with your code and requires zero third-party accounts.
  • For Non-Monetized Next.js Experiments: Pick Vercel Hobby, but remember to migrate away if you plan to monetize with ads.
  • For Sites Needing Built-In Forms: Pick Netlify, but set a bandwidth alert so you never hit their $55 overage charges.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use my own custom domain on free hosting?

Yes. All four platforms (Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Vercel, and Netlify) support custom apex domains (yourblog.com) and subdomains (www.yourblog.com) with free automated SSL certificates.

Will free hosting show third-party ads on my website?

No. None of these four developer platforms inject third-party ads into your code. The only ads that appear on your website are the ones you choose to add yourself (such as Google AdSense).

Is free static hosting good enough for SEO?

Static hosting is actually superior for SEO compared to cheap shared hosting. Because HTML is pre-rendered and served from edge CDN nodes, Time to First Byte (TTFB) is often under 50ms, earning higher Google Core Web Vitals and PageSpeed scores.
